note: Foundation for CA Community Colleges: CDSS's payment agent for child care contractor direct deposit and provider stipends (CDSS direct-deposit page: https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/child-care-and-development/direct-deposit). SCPRS value $25.9B is unconfirmed; Open FI$Cal shows ~$105M net paid FY2022-23..2024-25. Not procurement.

Advocates for Human Potential is DHCS's administrative entity for Prop 1 Bond BHCIP (~$4.4B competitive grants; Round 1 ~$3.3B); county funding agreements are signed with AHP under the DHCS prime contract, so the value is mostly grant money. https://www.gov.ca.gov/2025/05/30/building-on-billions-announced-earlier-this-month-governor-newsom-makes-800-million-available-in-new-prop-1-grants/

Starts with AHP's selection as BHCIP administrative entity (Sept 2021); original BHCIP rounds total ~$2.1-2.2B; $1.5B far exceeds any training contract, so the title understates it. Medium confidence: contract number not tied to a public document. https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/BHCIP/Pages/home.aspx

AHP administers Behavioral Health Bridge Housing (AB 179, Ch. 249/2022: $1.5B available through 2027-06-30, the contract's end date). https://counties.org/csac-bulletin-article/nearly-120-million-awarded-counties-behavioral-health-bridge-housing

AHP runs DSH's IST Infrastructure grants (~$468.8M one-time county grants for IST beds); value is the grant pool plus administration. https://www.dsh.ca.gov/About_Us/docs/DSH_2026-27_Governors_Budget_Highlights.pdf

AHP is CDSS's third-party grant and fiscal administrator for Community Care Expansion (AB 172 $805M + AB 178 $55M); county program funding agreements are signed with AHP under CDSS prime contract 21-3097. https://www.cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/cdss-programs/community-care-expansion ; https://public.destinyhosted.com/yolocdocs/2023/BOS/20230509_3583/13493_Att._A._Agreement.pdf

Per WIC 18999.97-18999.98 BDO is a CCE third-party administrator; counties sign CCE grant agreements with BDO (e.g. San Francisco r0587-25). Same CCE program envelope as AHP 78538. https://www.sfbos.org/sites/default/files/r0587-25.pdf

FCCC is CDSS's fiscal agent distributing AB 179 one-time child care provider stipends (ARPA-funded). http://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/child-care-and-development/subsidized-child-care-provider-stipends

FCCC issues the family child care supplemental rate payments ($289M through June 2023, AB 131 s.264). https://cdss.ca.gov/inforesources/child-care-and-development/child-care-provider-resources/supplemental-rate-payments

Public Consulting Group is DHCS's CalAIM PATH third-party administrator: per PCG, >$700M CITED grants, ~$500M Justice-Involved capacity grants, ~$200M TA Marketplace, ~$1.4B in total. https://publicconsultinggroup.com/insight/4793-public-consulting-groups-work-in-california-drives-measurable-expansion-of-healthcare-services-for-medi-cal-members/

CIBHS is the grant third-party administrator for CYBHI Evidence-Based / Community-Defined Practice grants ($381M-$429M authorized). Medium confidence: matched by program size and role. https://www.cibhs.org/projects/fiscal-administration-contracts-and-awards/

Sacramento County Office of Education is a grant administrator for CYBHI School-Linked Partnership and Capacity Grants; the K-12 pool is $400M, equal to the contract. https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/children-and-youth-behavioral-health-initiative-default/school-linked-partnerships-and-capacity-grants/

PACE organizations are paid monthly full-risk capitation per Medi-Cal enrollee: payment for beneficiaries' care, not a purchase for state operations. https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/services/ltc/Documents/PACE-State-Only-Contract-Boilerplate-2024.pdf

DMC-ODS State Plan Intergovernmental Agreement 2021-2027: the county is the Medi-Cal SUD plan and DHCS pays for beneficiaries' services. https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/file/sacramento-fy-2025-26-dmc-ods-findings-report-pdf/

DMC-ODS county intergovernmental agreement (Fresno), same structure as Sacramento 21-10032: Medi-Cal SUD service reimbursement. https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/file/sacramento-fy-2025-26-dmc-ods-findings-report-pdf/

Project Management and Funding Agreement HSR21-54 ($423,335,000) funds LA Metro's own Link US project (Prop 1A); Metro is lead agency. https://hsr.ca.gov/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Contracts-Expenditures-Report-September-26-2024-A11Y.pdf
CDSS transfers federal TANF to the Student Aid Commission to fund Cal Grants ($1,066M, LAO). https://www.lao.ca.gov/Publications/Report/4182

Medi-Cal fiscal intermediary (Gainwell, formerly DXC) is procurement, but $22.9B is ~30x public figures (DXC FI contract ~$710M through June 2028; FI costs ~$120-126M a year in the Medi-Cal Estimate). Start date 2026-12-01 on a FY16/17 agreement. Out of totals until corrected. https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/dataandstats/reports/mcestimates/Documents/2019_November_Estimate/N1999-Complete-Medi-Cal-Local-Estimate.pdf

Kings County jail-based competency treatment (~8 beds, Nov 2024-Jun 2025) registered at exactly $1,605,320,000; the prior Kings JBCT agreement (0000000000000000000094047) is $2,662,946 and DSH bed rates (~$565-623/day) put 8 beds at ~$1-2M: almost certainly $1,605,320 entered 1,000x. Out of totals until corrected. https://hanfordsentinel.com/news/local/kings-county-approves-jail-based-competency-treatment-program/article_6babda57-2843-5630-a80b-7acc55162c57.html

FCCC was CDSS's payment agent for the Golden State Stimulus: ~$711.1M paid to 1,185,135 SSI/SSP and CAPI recipients at $600 each (FTB report); the contract value is grant money. https://www.ftb.ca.gov/about-ftb/data-reports-plans/Golden-State-Stimulus-I-and-Golden-State-Grant-Payment-Report-2022.pdf
